item.title: Kundiawa police launch Christmas cleanliness operation
item.description: Simbu PPC Chief Superintendent Mazuc Rubiang addresses vendors and shoppers at Kundiawa market on the new cleanliness and dress code rules (Supplied) Anyone entering Kundiawa Town in dirty, filthy or unhygienic clothing risks being approached by police, removed from town, and sent home.
item.content:encoded:
Simbu PPC Chief Superintendent Mazuc Rubiang addresses vendors and shoppers at Kundiawa market on the new cleanliness and dress code rules (Supplied)

Anyone entering Kundiawa Town in dirty, filthy or unhygienic clothing risks being approached by police, removed from town, and sent home.

That is the warning from Simbu Provincial Police Commander, Chief Superintendent Mazuc M. Rumbiang, as police launch the Kundiawa Town Early Christmas and New Year Cleanliness Operation today.

PPC Rumbiang said for almost two years, police have taken the lead in organising community cleanathons in Kundiawa Town, which have improved the town's cleanliness, public behaviour, civic responsibility and law and order.

"As Christmas and New Year approaches, we are determined to maintain and further improve those standards," he said.

Under the operation, the public is reminded that:

- Everyone must wear clean, decent and presentable clothing when entering Kundiawa Town.

- Dirty, filthy and inappropriate dressing will not be encouraged.

- Members of the public must maintain personal hygiene and respect the cleanliness and dignity of the provincial capital.

- Visitors and travellers must uphold acceptable standards of public conduct while in town.

He also urged police and relevant authorities to enforce applicable public order and cleanliness requirements, and any enforcement action must be conducted lawfully and with respect for individual dignity.

PPC Rubiang said the new operation builds on past operations that have already worked well in Kundiawa.

These include the total ban on betel nut, smoking, street sales, the K5 boss crew, and drinking in public places and within the town vicinity.

He said those operations have helped make Kundiawa one of the cleanest and most peaceful towns in the country, and he is confident the new approach will also work.

In the enforcement warning, PPC Rubiang said anyone found roaming around Kundiawa Town in extremely dirty, filthy or unhygienic clothing will be approached by police for appropriate action under applicable public order laws.

"Some may find yourselves swimming at Wara Simbu and sent home immediately in wet clothes," he said.

He said where necessary, police may arrange for such individuals to be removed from the town and returned to their respective homes, in accordance with lawful procedures.

"Kundiawa is not a dumping ground. Anyone visiting or entering our provincial capital must maintain personal hygiene and dress decently. Kundiawa is our provincial capital. Its cleanliness, appearance and public image reflect who we are as the people of Simbu," he said.

He said everyone must take collective responsibility for maintaining a clean, peaceful, safe and presentable town throughout the festive season and beyond.

item.title: Police confiscate 248 rolls of marijuana at Kamkumung
item.description: Four women with suspected marijuana seized by Omili police and are now in police custody pending charges (Supplied) Lae police have confiscated 248 rolls of marijuana at Kamkumung Kona, with four female suspects detained in police custody pending charges.
item.content:encoded:
Four women with suspected marijuana seized by Omili police and are now in police custody pending charges (Supplied)

Lae police have confiscated 248 rolls of marijuana at Kamkumung Kona, with four female suspects detained in police custody pending charges.

Omili Police conducted the confiscation recently as police continue to address drug-related activities and rising community disturbances in Lae.

Meanwhile, police have confirmed that the instigator of last week's fight at West Taraka has been sentenced.

Lae Metropolitan Superintendent Chris Kunyanban said major crimes in the city remain manageable, but minor incidents such as mobile phone snatching and bag theft are increasingly triggering clashes among ethnic groups, gangs and peer groups, particularly in settlement communities.

Kunyanban attributed the growing violence to unemployment, school dropouts, alcohol abuse and drug consumption among young people.

"Unemployment has increased, and many youths are not in school and not employed. Many sit around settlements, consume illicit alcohol and smoke marijuana, and cause these fights," he said.

He also expressed concern over increasing alcohol abuse and drug use, particularly marijuana, warning that rising poverty could contribute to higher crime rates.

"The poverty level has increased, so will the crime," Kunyanban said.

The Metropolitan Superintendent thanked the court for recognising the interests of the peace-loving majority in West Taraka and sentencing the two suspects involved in the recent incident.

He urged residents of Lae and surrounding communities to exercise responsibility and use established processes to resolve disputes rather than resorting to violence.

"There is no need to escalate minor issues to serious crimes. We have processes in place to solve issues, and we must not act as primitives," he said.

Kunyanban further warned that police would hold individuals who instigate violence, as well as community leaders who fail to address disputes in accordance with the law, accountable.

item.title: CIS Buimo pilots inmates’ reintegration program in the country
item.description: Ex- inmate Rhoda John receives her carton of chicks from Commissioner Noel Sarei (Supplied) The Correctional Service (CIS) Buimo Institution is taking the lead in piloting an inmate reintegration program aimed at preparing prisoners to rebuild their lives and successfully return to their communities after serving their sentences.
item.content:encoded:
Ex- inmate Rhoda John receives her carton of chicks from Commissioner Noel Sarei (Supplied)

The Correctional Service (CIS) Buimo Institution is taking the lead in piloting an inmate reintegration program aimed at preparing prisoners to rebuild their lives and successfully return to their communities after serving their sentences.

Correctional Service Commissioner Noel Sarei officially launched Phase Two of the Pre-Release Program during his maiden visit to Buimo Correctional Institution recently.

Commissioner Sarei encouraged the 40 inmates who received start-up kits to help them establish small businesses after their release.

He told the recipients to remain resilient, take responsibility and make good use of the opportunity to rebuild their lives.

"I am reminding you that this is not an opportunity but a privilege that you must be grateful for. You must manage it wisely and produce positive results to ensure the continuity of the program," Sarei said.

He also commended Buimo Correctional Institution for going the extra mile in preparing inmates for life outside prison through practical training and business support.

Senior Inspector Hoxcy Pais Tibilio acknowledged the Australian-Papua New Guinea Government partnership for supporting the initiative and making it possible for inmates to receive financial and mindset training, as well as start-up capital.

"This program is made possible through the partnership between the Australian and Papua New Guinea governments, which has enabled us to provide financial and mindset training.

"We can now provide seed capital to inmates who have completed the training and are preparing to start their normal lives outside prison," Tibilio said.

Representing the 40 recipients was 27-year-old Rhoda John of Bundicamp, who plans to venture into poultry farming and eventually invest in rental properties.

John thanked Buimo Correctional Institution and its development partners for providing inmates with an opportunity to rebuild their lives after prison.

"I want to thank Buimo and all the other stakeholders who have contributed to creating this opportunity for us to rebuild our lives again after prison," she said.

She said she would rely on her family's support while working closely with the officers responsible for monitoring the program to ensure its success.

"I am banking on my family for their support and will continue working together with the officers in charge of monitoring to make sure this pilot program is a success, so others after us can also benefit," John said.

The Pre-Release Program includes two weeks of training delivered by partner agencies, covering financial management, mindset development and spiritual preparation to equip inmates for their return to society.

So far, 140 inmates have participated in the training, with the latest 40 recipients benefiting from start-up support under Phase Two of the program.

The initiative is expected to provide returning inmates with a pathway towards self-reliance, entrepreneurship and successful reintegration into their communities.

item.title: GFI assists with donations for children’s ward
item.description: Lae International school students with their gift hampers (Supplied) Goodman Fielder PNG (GFI) donated 60 stocks of gift hampers recently, to Lae International School to assist the students with their visitation to the Angau Children's ward this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Lae International school students with their gift hampers (Supplied)

Goodman Fielder PNG (GFI) donated 60 stocks of gift hampers recently, to Lae International School to assist the students with their visitation to the Angau Children's ward this weekend.

In its community engagement, it is supporting health, education, and community development through donations.

This initiative develops part of GFI's broader Hospital Christmas Donation Rollout, which will provide support to six general hospitals across Papua New Guinea in early December.

Trade Marketing & Insights Manager at Goodman Fielder PNG, Benjamin Raepa, explained that at Goodman Fielder, they believe in giving back to the communities that support the company.

"We are pleased to support Lae International School and look forward to extending our Hospital Christmas Donation Rollout to hospitals around the country as part of our ongoing commitment to community wellbeing."

Through programs such as these, GFI continues to invest in the wellbeing of communities and demonstrate its commitment to creating a positive and lasting impact across the country.

The school acknowledged and thanked GFI for their generous support for their planned boarders' visit to the children’s ward stated that this thoughtful contribution will enable their students to share practical support and kindness with children and families receiving care at the hospital.

item.title: Air Niugini flight makes emergency diversion to Davao after engine fire warning
item.description: Passengers are seen evacuating Air Niugini flight PX019 through the emergency exit slides after it safely landed in Davao, Philippines. (Image: Supplied) All passengers and crew on an Air Niugini flight from Hong Kong to Port Moresby are safe after the aircraft was diverted to the Philippines early this morning following a fire indication in one of its engines.
item.content:encoded:
Passengers are seen evacuating Air Niugini flight PX019 through the emergency exit slides after it safely landed in Davao, Philippines. (Image: Supplied)

All passengers and crew on an Air Niugini flight from Hong Kong to Port Moresby are safe after the aircraft was diverted to the Philippines early this morning following a fire indication in one of its engines.

The Boeing 767-300ER operating flight PX019 was carrying a PNG Government delegation returning from the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change [COP31] in Türkiye, along with other passengers.

The delegation included Environment Conservation and Climate Change Minister John Kaupa, Government Chief Secretary Ivan Pomaleu and officers from the Departments of Prime Minister, Foreign Affairs and Climate Change.

PNG High Commissioner to the Philippines, H.E. Stephen Pokanis, confirmed to NBC News after 7am this morning that the aircraft landed safely at Davao International Airport in Mindanao, Philippines, at around 2.30am local time [4:30am PNG Time].

He also confirmed that all passengers and crew, as well as the aircraft, landed safely.

In a message to the High Commissioner, Government Chief Secretary Ivan Pomaleu said the flight had encountered an incident during the journey that required it to divert to Davao.

"Excellency. Good morning. Just letting you know that PX 19 from Hong Kong encountered an incident midflight that required a flight diversion. We landed at Davao," the Chief Secretary said.

In a statement, Air Niugini confirmed that all passengers on the flight were safe and provided details of the incident and the arrangements being made for them.

"At approximately 1:30 am Port Moresby time on 21 November 2026, the pilots received a fire indication for the aircraft’s right engine. The crew followed standard procedures and shut down and secured the affected engine.

"The flight diverted to Davao International Airport and landed safely at 2.00am Port Moresby time. Passengers were evacuated and taken to the terminal.

"Our team is helping passengers to accommodation in Davao while we arrange for them to continue safely to Port Moresby. The welfare of our passengers and crew remains our priority. We will keep passengers informed directly and provide a further public update once onward travel arrangements are confirmed.

"We apologise for the disruption to their journeys and thank them for their patience while we make arrangements for them to reach Port Moresby. The safety of everyone who flies with Air Niugini remains our first priority."

item.title: 3rd City Rangers donate K40, 000 to URP
item.description: (L-R) Tabe Jugari- Patron and Sponsor of 03rd City Rangers and Principal of Stout Lawyers donating the K40,000 to Hagen Open MP and United Resources Party (URP) Leader William Duma witnessed by Cr. Samuel Maniat Ward 8 Councillor Hagen Urban LLG and Mosley Tika- Former Hagen Eagles player (Supplied) The 3rd City Rangers Rugby Football League Club in Mt Hagen has donated a total of K40,000 to the U
item.content:encoded:
(L-R) Tabe Jugari- Patron and Sponsor of 03rd City Rangers and Principal of Stout Lawyers donating the K40,000 to Hagen Open MP and United Resources Party (URP) Leader William Duma witnessed by Cr. Samuel Maniat Ward 8 Councillor Hagen Urban LLG and Mosley Tika- Former Hagen Eagles player (Supplied)

The 3rd City Rangers Rugby Football League Club in Mt Hagen has donated a total of K40,000 to the United Resources Party (URP) led by Hagen Open MP and party leader William Duma.

The donation was made jointly by the 03rd City Rangers and its patron and sponsor, Tabe Jugari, the principal of Stout Lawyers.

According to the club, K20,000 was contributed by the 03rd City Rangers, while another K20,000 was donated by Mr Jugari in his personal capacity as the club’s patron and sponsor.

The money was formally presented to URP Leader and Hagen Open MP William Duma in Port Moresby.

"The donation is a show of support for the URP and its leadership, particularly its vision for the development of Papua New Guinea, Mt Hagen and Western Highlands Province," said Stout Lawyers Principal Mr. Jugari.

Jugari stress the Rangers also believe in building a strong partnership with the party and supporting development that benefits young people.

Hagen Open MP, William Duma says this is the first time his party has received support of this kind from a sporting team.

"This is the very first of its kind for our Party to receive support from a sporting team.

"I have supported sports especially rugby league, for a longtime even before I entered politics and throughout my political career," MP Duma said.

He describes the donation as a significant show of confidence and trust from young people in Mt Hagen and says it reflects their belief in the URP's vision for practical and people-centred leadership.

Duma also commended the 03rd City Rangers for their discipline, unity and achievements.

"I commend 03rd City Rangers for their discipline, unity and outstanding achievement and I look forward to a continued partnership in promoting youth development, sport and nation building," added Duma.

The 03rd City Rangers represents Wards One to Eight of the Hagen Urban Local Level Government (LLG), as well as Hagen Rural LLG and Western Highlands Province.

The team recently competed in the Rigo Rice Cup 2026, where it was declared one of the dual winners.

item.title: K3 Billion in lost log export and income tax revenues
item.description: About 3-billion-kina is estimated to have been lost in export revenue and income tax between 2023-2025 in the country’s logging forestry sector. This was revealed through a study conducted by the community advocacy group ACT NOW which showed the cost of logs exported from PNG were much lower than its import cost in China.
item.content:encoded:
About 3-billion-kina is estimated to have been lost in export revenue and income tax between 2023-2025 in the country’s logging forestry sector.

This was revealed through a study conducted by the community advocacy group ACT NOW which showed the cost of logs exported from PNG were much lower than its import cost in China.

Campaign Manager Eddie Tanago said this is a serious issue that must be looked into immediately by the government and other relevant authorities.

“The government, the relevant authorities really need to pay attention to the alerts, the red flags that civil societies like us or any other concerned body because these are all very important issues to the country.

“We have been talking about issues of illegal laundering, illegal logging, issues of money laundering, issues of forest crime and yet, these are not acted on.

“The banking sector is involved as well to facilitate, to keep the accounts of those who are doing business, the real estate agents, the lawyers, the accountants. It is a whole heap of bodies that provides the conducive environment for such business to flourish,” Tanago said.

Similarly, a previous report released by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime from 2018 to 2022 revealed a discrepancy of over 6-billion-kina between export values from PNG and import values to China.

Mr Tanago said this trend over the past years without action by relevant government bodies is very concerning.

He said such dealings which may involve transfer pricing, tax evasion is closely linked to money laundering within the logging industry, and is straining the country’s economy, especially in this El Nino period when communities, schools and hospitals are in immense need of funding.

The Act NOW Campaign Manager is calling on the relevant stakeholders and banks to take corrective measures to immediately rectify and prevent other similar occurrences.

“We are all in an El Nino season and we are in dire need of funding. Our communities really need those monies. And we are talking about potential revenue for Papua New Guinea that is going down the drain.

“The call now is to, yes, the government, its relevant authorities, including sectors that play a key role in enabling such businesses to flourish. We need to act. Especially we need the government to really step up and push for this and the banks as well,” Tanago said.

PNG Forest Authority will be releasing a statement on this.

item.title: Mothers in Kundiawa receive free life skills training
item.description: Mothers from Ward 3 in Kundiawa Urban LLG celebrate after completing their life skills training and thank XSPI and PNG Working Group (NBC News) Twelve mothers in Ward 3 area in the Kundiawa Urban LLG are not the same after receiving free life skills training.
item.content:encoded:
Mothers from Ward 3 in Kundiawa Urban LLG celebrate after completing their life skills training and thank XSPI and PNG Working Group (NBC News)

Twelve mothers in Ward 3 area in the Kundiawa Urban LLG are not the same after receiving free life skills training.

The training was delivered under the Family Economic Empowerment program under the Drought Outreach Program, supported by XSPI of Australian NGO and PNG Working Group.

Livelihood specialist and lead trainer Agnes Siune said the skills will help mothers turn their staple food into flour and store it for future use when El Nino or disaster happens.

She said it will also pave the way for them to venture into markets, and to know how to make a balanced diet and cook using different recipes.

In a small but significant gathering, the mothers who attended the training left with something they did not have before — skills to feed their family and make money.

Ms Siune said she has trained more than 30 women in the six districts in Simbu, who have now become trainers and are training mothers in the villages of Simbu province.

She said mothers in the villages who have been trained are now making tapioca cake, sweet potato (kaukau) muffin, banana cake, cookies and organic spice and soup.

Apolonia Gena, a mother of six who attended the training, thanked lead trainer Agnes Siune for bringing the skills to the mothers.

She said this life skills training will stay with them forever.

"SME training takes forever without favorable outcome. Training we receive is simple, productive and will help us in many ways," she said.

Lucas Wamne said all mothers, especially housewives and young women who do nothing in the village or town, should gain such unique skills and venture into small market to sustain themselves.

Mothers from Ward 3 area in Kundiawa Urban LLG all urged the local-level and district development authority to assist them with locally made oven and hand grill to put into practice what they have learnt.
